In detail

Praha 5 is one of Prague's 57 official mestske casti (city districts). Policie CR (the Czech national police) recorded 17,693 incidents here in 2024 across a population of 97,109 residents — a rate of 18,220 incidents per 100,000 residents, roughly 1.4× the citywide district average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central/tourist district can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential district can show a low rate simply by having few incidents relative to its population. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Prague — real Policie CR incident data and real CSU population figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Praha 5 safe?

Wandroz currently rates Praha 5 in Prague as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Prague. This rating is derived from Policie ČR's official crime statistics (kriminalita.policie.gov.cz) — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats. The source data has no day/night breakdown, so this single rating applies at any time of day rather than being a distinct night-specific figure.

Does Praha 5's rating differ between day and night?

No — Praha 5's source data has no time-of-day breakdown, so the same rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Prague) is shown for both day and night rather than Wandroz inventing a separate night figure it doesn't actually have.

Is Praha 5 a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Praha 5's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Prague) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
